title: Missing index
summary: Repeatable lookups that no index covers: claims aging by payer and submission date, and visits by reason code. Each call scans its table, and the optimizer records a missing-index suggestion. The story is before, recommendation, action, after: the remediation (scenarios/missing-index/remediation.sql) is reviewed and applied by a person, never automatically.

intensity.description: Pace: a lookup about once a second per session at 1, about 50 per second at 10.

notes.T3: Azure SQL Database may also raise its own CREATE INDEX tuning recommendation after enough executions.

expectedHubSignals.signal: SqlServerCPUUtilization and logical reads higher than the baseline
A missing-index or query-tuning finding with the index as the recommended action
expectedHubSignals.note: Preview; coverage by target is undocumented (ADR 0013).

expectedSymptoms: Every claims-aging lookup scans care.claims; every reason-code lookup scans care.appointments
sys.dm_db_missing_index_details suggests (payer_code, submitted_on) INCLUDE (billed_amount, claim_status) on care.claims and (reason_code, scheduled_start) on care.appointments
After a person applies remediation.sql, the same lookups seek and their reads drop sharply
queryLevelEvidence: Query Store: the lookups' plans before and after the index (forced plans aren't used)
The plan's MissingIndex element and sys.dm_db_missing_index_group_stats (needs VIEW SERVER STATE or VIEW DATABASE STATE)
reset: The lookups only read. Reset with --undo-remediation (or EXEC demo.usp_undo_missing_index_remediation) drops the two remediation indexes, so the scenario starts again from 'before'.
